title: From Thee, My God, My Joys Shall Rise
description: From Thee, My God, My Joys Shall Rise in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 75, headed “Spiritual and eternal joys; or, The beatific sight of Christ”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: From thee, my God, my joys shall rise, And run e-ter-nal rounds, Be-yond the lim-its of the skies And all cre-a-ted bounds.

lines: From thee, my God, my joys shall rise,
Beyond the limits of the skies
The holy triumphs of my soul
There, where my blessed Jesus reigns
Millions of years my wondering eyes
Sweet Jesus, every smile of thine
And thousand tastes of new delight
Haste, my beloved, fetch my soul
Fly, for my spirit longs to see

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
